title.narrative: Uganda: Community Justice Programme - Phase II (CJP II)

description.narrative: 1) To empower grassroot communities to claim and uphold their rights. 2) To ensure justice services are responsive to the needs and priorities of justice seekers. 3) To improve responsiveness of justice services for women and children. 4) To improve effectiveness of justice accountability and feedback mechanisms.

Direct beneficiaries: The Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (MoJCA), the Ministry of Local Government, the Judiciary, the Judiciary Service Commission, the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the Office of Directorate of Public Prosecutions (ODPP), the Uganda Prisons Service (UPS), the Uganda Police Force (UPF), the Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (MoGLSD), the Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control, the Uganda Law Reform Commission (ULRC), the Equal Opportunities Commission (EOC), the Uganda Human Rights Commission (UHRC), the National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA), and strategic non-state Justice, Law and Order Sector (JLOS) institutions, such as the Uganda Law Society (ULS) and community level JLOS structures, such as Local Council Courts (LCCs), District Chain-Linked Committees (DCC), Justice Centres Uganda (JCU), Human Rights Desks, legal volunteers and social workers engaged by state led-legal aid service providers.Indirect beneficiaries: Community members.
The project aims to enhance the accessibility, quality and sustainability of justice services delivered for justice seekers in Uganda.
